title: Bulgaria – Visa and Travel Information for Serbian Citizens

embassy_in_serbia.name: Embassy of the Republic of Bulgaria in Belgrade

visa_eligibility.serbian_citizens: Serbian citizens holding a valid biometric passport do NOT need a visa to enter Bulgaria for stays up to 90 days within any 180-day period. Travel documents must have been issued within the last 10 years and remain valid for at least 3 months after the planned departure date. Non-biometric passport holders and holders of emergency travel documents in transit require a standard Bulgarian visa.
visa_eligibility.other_nationals: Third-country nationals residing in Serbia who are not Serbian citizens must apply for a Bulgarian visa at the Embassy/Consular Office in Belgrade. Citizens of EU/EEA/Schengen states are exempt. Citizens of countries covered by visa-free agreements with Bulgaria are also exempt.

processing_times.notes: Short-stay Visa C: approximately 15 calendar days. Long-stay Visa D: approximately 35 business days, up to 6 months in complex cases. Applications may be submitted no earlier than 3 months (6 months for Visa D) before the intended travel date.

application_location.center: Consular Office of the Embassy of the Republic of Bulgaria
application_location.booking: Contact the consular office directly by phone (+381 11 324 7675) or email (Consulate.Belgrade@mfa.bg) to schedule an appointment. No third-party visa application center (VFS Global) identified for Serbia.

fee_exemptions: Holders of diplomatic and official passports

required_documents_all_applicants: Completed and signed visa application form
Valid travel document (passport) – issued within the last 10 years, valid at least 3 months beyond intended stay
Photocopy of the bio-data page of the travel document
Photocopy of all previous Bulgarian, Schengen, UK, and US visas (if any)
One recent color photograph (3.5 cm × 4.5 cm, light-colored background)
Travel medical insurance with minimum coverage of €30,000, valid for the entire stay and all Schengen states
Proof of accommodation (hotel booking, invitation letter, or rental agreement)
Proof of sufficient financial means (min. €50/day; overall not less than €500) – bank statements or similar
Proof of round-trip or onward travel (flight/bus/train reservation or itinerary)
Vehicle registration/technical passport (if traveling by car)
additional_documents_by_nationality: Applicants with previous refusals must disclose this on the application form
Non-Serbian residents in Serbia must provide proof of legal residence permit

required: Notarized parental consent from the non-accompanying parent(s) if traveling with one parent
Court order or legal document if applicable (e.g., sole custody)
Authorization documents for minors traveling unaccompanied
documents_for_minors.note: Minors must appear in person for biometric data collection where required.

tourism: Confirmed hotel/accommodation booking or invitation from host
business: Invitation letter from Bulgarian business partner on company letterhead
Proof of business registration of inviting company
Letter from employer confirming purpose and duration of trip
family_or_private_visit: Invitation letter from host in Bulgaria (notarized if required)
Proof of host's legal residence or citizenship in Bulgaria
medical_treatment: Medical referral or appointment confirmation from Bulgarian medical institution
Proof of payment or financial guarantee for treatment
transit: Valid visa or residence permit for the destination country
Note: Serbian citizens with biometric passports do not need a transit visa for airport transit through Bulgaria

employees: Employment contract or letter from employer
Employer confirmation of leave/business trip approval
Recent payslips or bank statements showing regular income
entrepreneurs: Bank statements showing business activity and sufficient funds
students: Proof of scholarship or financial support
retirees: Pension certificate or proof of pension payments

special_provisions: Since March 31, 2024, Bulgaria is a full Schengen member. Bulgarian short-stay visas (Type C) are now valid throughout the entire Schengen Area. Serbian citizens holding biometric passports are visa-exempt for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. ETIAS authorization will be required for Serbian citizens once the European Travel Information and Authorisation System launches (expected late 2026) – this is not a visa but an online pre-screening requirement. Travelers entering Bulgaria by car must have a valid electronic road vignette. Currency amounts exceeding €10,000 must be declared at customs upon entry.
